verdict_3_vs_4.bottom_line: Plan on a good 3.5-bit (Q3_K_XL / IQ3_KS / DQ3 class) scoring 95-99% of the 4-bit on coding, and a 3.0-bit (IQ3_XXS class) 90-97%. But the 3-bit drifts 3-6x further from the original per token, so long agentic runs and hard reasoning fall off faster than the benchmark ratio suggests. For DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and Kimi K2-Thinking+ the 4-bit IS the full model (quantization-aware trained), so there '3 vs 4' means '3 vs full'; no coding benchmark of a 3-bit V4/V4.1 exists yet (unknown).

inferred.target: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: coding-hot experts at native 4-bit (MXFP4, untouched), the rest at ~2.25-bit (IQ2_XXS gate/up + Q2_K down)
inferred.method: Linear in coverage: error ~= (share of routing picks that land on 2-bit experts) x (error of the all-2-bit build). All-2-bit V4.1 = KL 0.260, PPL +14.9%, top-1 78.3% (Lucebox); hot share 74% (range 50-85%) from GLM-5.3-Flash chat; hot set = 100/288 of experts. KL ~0.07 sits where a uniform ~3-bit V4 build sits (AtomicChat delta-KLD 0.050-0.093 at 3.2-2.9 expert bits), so retention is read off the 3-bit row of the curve.
caveats: V4.1 routing concentration is UNMEASURED (384 experts, 6 active); the 74% is GLM-5.3-Flash chat traffic
at the same bytes this is about equal to a uniform ~3-bit build; the gain is speed (hot experts in VRAM), not quality per byte
pick the hot set from coding traffic with router-weighted saliency, never raw frequency or C4/chat text (REAP)
frequency allocation only helps when routing is unbalanced (QuantMoE-Bench): measure V4.1's balance first
stock llama.cpp cannot give per-expert types inside one merged tensor; needs a fork (Lucebox PR 593 codebooks, hot-expert cache PR) or our split engine

inferred.target: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: coding-hot experts at ~3-bit, the rest at ~2.25-bit
inferred.method: Same coverage model: 0.74 x (3-bit hot error) + 0.26 x 0.260. 3-bit hot error = V4 Flash 0731 delta-KLD over native at 3.20 and 2.91 expert bits (0.050, 0.093). No 3-bit V4.1 measurement exists. Result KL 0.105-0.136 matches a uniform ~2.7-2.8-bit V4 build (delta 0.100 at 2.79), better than uniform 2.5 (0.178).
caveats: requantizing native MXFP4 hot experts to 3-bit throws away lossless bits for ~25% less hot-set memory; worth it only if the hot set then fits VRAM and the 4-bit one does not
PPL range is our scaling of the all-2-bit +14.9% by the KL ratio

inferred.method: Measured directly, then mapped to coding with the curve. GGUF near 3.0: unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS 3.01 bpw KLD 0.284, top-1 81.63%; AesSedai IQ3_S 3.11 PPL +22.88%; GSQ-RCO 3.0 (2.94 bpw) MMLU-Pro 96.9%, PPL +9.07%, math -11.6%. EXL3 3.05: KLD 0.0681 where AWQ int4 scores 0.0565 and UD-IQ4_XS 0.0615 in the same harness, so EXL3 3.05 ~ a GGUF 4-bit. Coding range from V3.1 Aider UD-IQ3_XXS 93.3% and the 3-10x coding multiplier on the 3.1% MMLU-Pro loss.
caveats: GLM is BF16-native (no QAT), so even 4-bit loses: Q4_K_M PPL +1.83%
GLM-family PPL rises faster per bit than DeepSeek in ubergarm's tables (IQ2_KL ~3.0: GLM-4.6 +20%, GLM-5.1 +15% vs V3.1 +8.5%)
EXL3 is GPU-only: 3.05 bpw x 320B ~ 122 GB must sit in VRAM
